description: Four newly authored question candidates generated in response to the three source-flagged ambiguous original NBF Unit7 end MCQs 3/5/10; original book and all 274 historical source identities preserved.

sourceBasis.book: NBF Grade XI Physics of Solids, printed p.125 original scan, visually reopened 2026-11-27

candidates.stem: When solids are classified by their dominant bonding arrangement, how is crystalline silicon most appropriately described?
options: A molecular solid consisting of isolated Si molecules
An ionic solid formed from silicon cations and anions
A metallic solid with delocalized conduction electrons
candidates.teacherReviewFocus: Explicit bonding classification avoids confusing diamond-cubic lattice periodicity with the type of bonding; check that the item is appropriate to the B-22 scope.

candidates.stem: A wire with an initial cross-sectional area of 2.0 mm² carries a steady axial tensile force of 30 N. Taking engineering stress (force divided by the initial area), what is the tensile stress?
candidates.teacherReviewFocus: Engineering stress uses the stated INITIAL area, not unknown true/deformed area. The wire is not claimed to have doubled its length or remained linearly elastic at large strain.

candidates.stem: During the proportional elastic range, an object obeys F = kx. On a graph with force F on the vertical axis and extension x on the horizontal axis, how does the gradient behave?
options: It remains constant and equals the stiffness k
It increases in direct proportion to x
It equals the extension x at every point
It is always negative and equals −1/k
candidates.teacherReviewFocus: The gradient is constant ONLY in the stated proportional Hookean range; this item is supportive graph knowledge, not direct evidence for official B-27 area-under-graph work Application.

candidates.stem: A spring obeys F = kx with k = 200 N/m throughout the stretch from x = 0 to x = 0.10 m. Using the area under the force–extension graph, how much work is done in stretching the spring?
candidates.teacherReviewFocus: The graph area is triangular, with the zero-extension origin, force vertical and extension horizontal; the question is a separate B-27 application candidate, not the source's original graph-gradient MCQ.
